t: A tiny, very cheap chip for homemade USB keyboards, knobs, and buttons.
steps: Buy an Adafruit CH552 QT Py from Adafruit or a Ham CH552 Micro from Tindie.
Install the free Arduino IDE on your computer.
Add the ch55xduino board package through the Boards Manager.
Set up the driver on Windows or the udev rule on Linux as the ch55xduino guide shows.
Hold the bootloader button and plug the board in with a USB-C cable.
Open the Blink example and upload it.
Try a USB keyboard example next and watch it type into a text file.
meta: Wild Open. From $2.50. A few stores.
